newsitem.title: UK: S. Africa's Oribi oilfield delivers first cargo.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa's Oribi oilfield delivers first cargo.

text.p: South Africa's state oil firm Soekor delivered its first cargo from the newly commissioned Oribi oilfield into Cape Town on Saturday, the company said.
The 650,000 barrel cargo has been purchased by Caltex Oil SA for its Cape Town refinery.
The crude represents South Africa's first significant production after a 30-year search for oil.
Oribi has been in full production at a rate of 24,000 barrels a day (bpd), slightly higher than planned, since coming onstream on May 12.
Oribi, a low sulphur crude comparable to British North Sea Brent blend, is owned 80 percent by Soekor with Energy Africa holding a 20 percent stake.
The field, with estimated recoverable reserves of just 20 million barrels, will provide about six percent of South African oil requirements for up to four years.

It is expected to form the nucleus of a sequential development of several smaller fields in the Bredasdorp Basin off South Africa's southern coast, which should add extra recoverable reserves of 15-40 million barrels.
